Sasha — thanks for the diagram and the proposed window. Below is the acceptance checklist Redwood needs completed before we approve traffic shifts. I split out what must be validated in staging vs. what we confirm in the live canary window.

Redwood acceptance checklist (high level):
- Staging validation (pre-cutover, non-prod):
  - Model service health: inference node autoscale triggers in staging for target QPS (smoke test at 3x expected canary load).
  - KV cache warming test: validated prefix cache population and hit-rate >= 60% for representative prompts.
  - TLS/mTLS: cert chain verification, client auth testing against sample client certs.
  - Metrics & logs: Prometheus metrics from edge cluster + traceID propagation to Redwood tracing (sample traces in staging).
  - BGP session stability: verify BGP flaps = 0 in 10m test window.

- Live canary acceptance (during 1st traffic shift):
  - Canary target: 5% of production traffic for 15 minutes with ramp steps (5m increments).
  - Latency SLO check: p95 within 1.2x baseline and no >5% increase in error rate.
  - Token billing sanity: confirm token accounting matches sample sessions in logs.
  - Failover validation: verify automatic fallback to hosted region if edge cluster returns 5xx or BGP withdraws routes.
  - Operator runbook validated: manual rollback (step-by-step) completes in <= 10 minutes in test.

- Post-cutover validation: 1 hour and 24-hour checks for telemetry drift, model quality alerts, and billing deltas.

Attachments referenced: isolated_edge_acceptance_checklist_v1.xlsx (I attached a short XLSX checklist you can fill during handoff)

Irene and Karthik, can you add any infra-level gating items (network/egress, KMS access) — high level only; we want to keep Sasha's checklist tight.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding infra-level acceptance items:
- KMS/KRACK: confirm HSM key wrap policy allows Redwood agent to request ephemeral keys; test key retrieval in staging with egress rules applied.
- Egress proofing: ensure allowed egress CIDR list includes Redwood telemetry endpoints (metrics, traces, cost-aggregation). Provide explicit IP CIDR set.
- NAT hairpin / SNAT behavior: verify service IP preservation for intra-cluster calls; regression test for sidecar-to-sidecar connectivity.
- Load balancer health checks: 30s probes aligned with app-level readiness to avoid premature removal.
- Ops credentials: provide temporary operator role for Redwood on the first canary (role expires after 48h).

I'll include minimal acceptance rows in the XLSX so it's easy to tick off.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

2) Routing window: we prefer the 02:00–04:00 local window; please confirm your team can accept a 30-minute rollback pause if p95 breaches.
3) Observability links: share Prometheus scrape endpoints and trace sample IDs (we requested a couple sample traces earlier) so our health dashboards display immediately after canary start.

Also attached a tiny playbook snippet for traffic-shift rollback (traffic-shift-playbook.docx) — please integrate into your runbook and return an updated PDF.

Thanks,
